list.name: Citric Acid Monohydrate - 5000g
list.description:
Citric Acid Monohydrate

Other Names: 2-Hydroxy-1,2,3-propane-tricarboxylic acid monohydrate
CAS Number: 5949-29-1
EC Number: 201-069-1
Chemical Formula: C₆H₈O₇·H₂O
Molar Mass: 210.14 g/mol
Appearance: White, crystalline solid

Chemical and Physical Properties

  • Density: ~1.54 g/cm³

  • Melting Point: 100–104°C (loss of water of crystallization)

  • Boiling Point: Decomposes before boiling

  • Solubility in Water: Highly soluble (590 g/L at 20°C)

  • Solubility in Other Solvents: Soluble in ethanol and acetone

  • Odor: Odorless

  • pH (1% solution): ~2.2

Applications

  • Chemical Industry: Used as a chelating agent and pH regulator in various formulations.

  • Laboratory Use: Employed as a buffer component and acidulant in experiments.

  • Cleaning Products: Acts as a descaling agent and ingredient in eco-friendly cleaners.

  • Cosmetics and Personal Care: Used as a pH adjuster and mild exfoliant.

  • Photography and Textile Processing: Occasionally used in dyeing and photographic baths.

Safety

Signal Word: Warning

GHS Hazard Statements

H315 (14.2%): Causes skin irritation [Warning Skin corrosion/irritation]

H319 (93.2%): Causes serious eye irritation [Warning Serious eye damage/eye irritation]

H335 (45.3%): May cause respiratory irritation [Warning Specific target organ toxicity, single exposure; Respiratory tract irritation]

Precautionary Statement Codes

P261, P264, P264+P265, P271, P280, P302+P352, P304+P340, P305+P351+P338, P319, P321, P332+P317, P337+P317, P362+P364, P403+P233, P405, and P501

Handling and Storage

  • Storage Conditions: Store in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from incompatible substances such as strong oxidizers.

  • Handling Precautions: Avoid generating dust. Use suitable protective equipment when handling large quantities.

list.name: Sodium Dichromate
list.shortDescription: ⚠️ EU: This product is  classified as CMR in category 1A/1B Annex VI. CLP Regulation (EC) No. 1272/2008 and therefore can only be purchased by registered business or government entities.
list.description:
Sodium Dichromate
Other Names: Chromic acid disodium salt, Sodium bichromate, Bichromate of soda

CAS Number: 10588-01-9
Sum Formula: Na₂Cr₂O₇
Molar Mass: 261.97 g/mol
Appearance: Orange to red crystalline solid

Sodium dichromate is a highly water-soluble, inorganic oxidizing agent containing chromium in the hexavalent state (Cr⁶⁺). It is commonly used in industrial and laboratory applications requiring strong oxidation, particularly in the synthesis of organic and inorganic chemicals, corrosion inhibition, and metal finishing.

Chemical and Physical Properties
Density: 2.52 g/cm³
Melting Point: 356.7°C (decomposes)
Boiling Point: Not applicable (decomposes)
Solubility in Water: Highly soluble (73 g/100 mL at 20°C)
Solubility in Other Solvents: Slightly soluble in alcohol
Odor: Odorless

Applications
Oxidizing Agent: Used in organic synthesis for oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes.
Corrosion Inhibitor: Applied in metal surface treatments and passivation.
Pigments and Dyes: Precursor for various chromium-based pigments.
Tanning Industry: Employed in leather processing (now largely replaced due to toxicity).
Laboratory Reagent: Used in analytical chemistry and qualitative testing.

Safety


Signal Word: Danger

GHS Hazard Statements

H272 (98.5%): May intensify fire; oxidizer [Danger Oxidizing liquids; Oxidizing solids]

H301 (> 99.9%): Toxic if swallowed [Danger Acute toxicity, oral]

H312 (98.5%): Harmful in contact with skin [Warning Acute toxicity, dermal]

H314 (> 99.9%): Causes severe skin burns and eye damage [Danger Skin corrosion/irritation]

H317 (> 99.9%): May cause an allergic skin reaction [Warning Sensitization, Skin]

H330 (> 99.9%): Fatal if inhaled [Danger Acute toxicity, inhalation]

H334 (> 99.9%): May cause allergy or asthma symptoms or breathing difficulties if inhaled [Danger Sensitization, respiratory]

H340 (> 99.9%): May cause genetic defects [Danger Germ cell mutagenicity]

H350 (99.1%): May cause cancer [Danger Carcinogenicity]

H360 (94%): May damage fertility or the unborn child [Danger Reproductive toxicity]

H372 (98.5%): Causes damage to organs through prolonged or repeated exposure [Danger Specific target organ toxicity, repeated exposure]

H400 (> 99.9%): Very toxic to aquatic life [Warning Hazardous to the aquatic environment, acute hazard]

H410 (> 99.9%): Very toxic to aquatic life with long lasting effects [Warning Hazardous to the aquatic environment, long-term hazard]

Precautionary Statement Codes

P203, P210, P220, P233, P260, P261, P264, P270, P271, P272, P273, P280, P284, P301+P316, P301+P330+P331, P302+P352, P302+P361+P354, P304+P340, P305+P354+P338, P316, P317, P318, P319, P320, P321, P330, P333+P317, P342+P316, P362+P364, P363, P370+P378, P391, P403, P403+P233, P405, and P501

 

Handling and Storage
Storage Conditions: Store in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from combustible materials, reducing agents, and acids.
Handling Precautions: Handle with extreme caution due to carcinogenicity and oxidizing nature. Use full PPE and operate in a chemical fume hood or controlled environment.

list.name: Potassium Citrate
list.description:
POTASSIUM CITRATE

Other Names: Potassium salt of citric acid, potassium citrate, tripotassium citrate

CAS Number: 866-84-2
Chemical Formula: C₆H₅K₃O₇
Molar Mass: 306.39 g/mol
Appearance: White solid, powder, granules or crystals

Potassium citrate is the potassium salt of citric acid. The product is most commonly supplied as a white powder, granules or crystals and is readily soluble in water. It is characterized by buffering properties and the ability to influence the pH of aqueous solutions. It may be used as a reagent, a component of technical formulations, an auxiliary substance in chemical mixtures and a source of potassium and citrate ions.

Chemical and Physical Properties

Form: Solid, powder, granules or crystals
Color: White
Odor: Odorless or slightly characteristic
Solubility in Water: Readily soluble
Solubility in Organic Solvents: Limited
Chemical Character: Organic potassium salt of citric acid
pH of Aqueous Solution: Usually slightly alkaline
Properties: Buffering compound, source of potassium and citrate ions
Stability: Stable under normal storage conditions, protect from moisture

Applications

Laboratory Use: Used as a reagent, buffer solution component and auxiliary material in chemical procedures.

pH Adjustment: Applied for correction and stabilization of the pH of aqueous solutions.

Technical Formulations: May be used as a component of mixtures requiring the presence of a citrate salt.

Source of Potassium Ions: Provides K⁺ ions in a readily soluble form.

Source of Citrate Ions: Used where the presence of citrate anions in solution is required.

Buffer Systems: Applied in mixtures where maintaining a defined pH range is important.

Not intended for food, pharmaceutical or cosmetic applications unless the product has the appropriate grade and documentation required for such uses.

Handling and Storage

Store in a tightly closed container in a dry, cool and well-ventilated place. Protect from moisture, direct sunlight and product contamination. Close the container tightly after use to reduce caking and maintain product quality. Keep away from chemically incompatible substances
